name: Kyrgyzstan
summary_text: Kyrgyzstan is dangerous for trans visitors — once Central Asia's relative haven, now regressing. In 2023-2024 Kyrgyzstan adopted two discriminatory laws targeting the LGBTI community and restricting LGBTI organisations, accompanied by homophobic/transphobic MP rhetoric; TGEU records Kyrgyzstan (2021) among the countries that removed legal gender recognition entirely (the 2020 Civil Status Acts law blocks birth-certificate changes). Same-sex conduct is legal (1998), but police abuse and extortion of LGBT people are documented, and the community (Kyrgyz Indigo) operates under pressure. For a visitor: no expression statute, but LGR removal + police extortion culture + active anti-LGBT political campaign make outing risky.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Kyrgyzstan: two discriminatory laws (2023-2024) target the LGBTI community and restrict organisations, amid homophobic political rhetoric; since 2021 trans people cannot obtain legal recognition (Law on Civil Acts amendments); in 2024 Article 47 of the Health Law was amended to bar gender-transition-related medical examination or treatment until age 25 (previously 18); ECOM data show high stigma from law enforcement and healthcare workers, with police abuse of power.

sources.title: Trans Rights Index & Map 2024 reveals polarisation in trans rights in Europe and Central Asia - TGEU - Trans Europe and Central AsiaTGEU – Trans Europe and Central Asia
sources.claim_summary: TGEU Trans Rights Index & Map 2024 launch (May 2024): documents polarisation in trans rights across Europe and Central Asia - progress in some countries (Greece, Iceland topping the ranking) and alarming regressions elsewhere, notably Russia's July 2023 ban on medical and legal transition; two new indicators added for 2024.

sources.title: Kyrgyzstan | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex activity decriminalised 1998 (equal age of consent 16); 2016 constitutional amendment bans same-sex marriage; the provision allowing some trans people to change markers was removed in 2020; in early 2026 an MP proposed a bill defining sex as immutable, explicitly banning legal gender recognition and prohibiting any interventions on minors; follows the 2023-2024 'silencing' laws.

ECOM study (2024) on trans people's access to medical services including HIV prevention and HRT across the EECA region (with country coordinators for Georgia, Armenia, Ukraine, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Kyrgyzstan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan) - includes information for trans migrants.

sources.title: World Report 2020: Kyrgyzstan | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW World Report 2020, Kyrgyzstan chapter: includes a Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity section - documents the worsening environment for LGBT people, including the 'gay propaganda' bill and violence against women.

sources.title: Curtain Falls On Bishkek's Lone LGBT Club Amid Worsening Atmosphere
sources.claim_summary: RFE/RL (June 2017): 'Curtain Falls On Bishkek's Lone LGBT Club Amid Worsening Atmosphere' - the London club in Bishkek closed; founder Olesya: 'people don't understand what a gay club is... they think we are doing something pornographic. But if they came and saw that it is just a normal club... it would be OK.'

sources.title: 'All of us will be victims at some point': why Bishkek's only gay club closed | Cities | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (Oct 2017): 'All of us will be victims at some point': why Bishkek's only gay club closed - the Kyrgyz capital was long a liberal beacon in Central Asia until the 'LGBT propaganda' ban; with attacks and rapes on the rise, the community is scared.
